comment: The section defines the scope at the level of a national health system but does not fully address subnational, regional, cross-border, or multi-country architectures. This may be problematic for decentralised countries where health-system authority and infrastructure are distributed.

anchor.note: p.24-25 l.Lines 29-41 read as the printed page; section 2.1 agrees

public.text: The section defines the scope at the level of a national health system but does not fully address subnational, regional, cross-border, or multi-country architectures. This may be problematic for decentralised countries where health-system authority and infrastructure are distributed.
public.suggestedRevision: State that the national level is the principal frame of reference, while components and governance may be realised nationally, subnationally, regionally, or through federated arrangements according to constitutional and institutional context.
